assessment.nobel_worthiness: Changed how economists and policymakers understand technology, trade and labour demand. The task-based approach, the skill-premium work and the local labour-market evidence on trade exposure link directly to open questions about technological change and distributional costs. The empirical designs are widely taught and have been applied well beyond the original settings.
assessment.attribution: The task framework is most closely tied to Autor. The trade-shock evidence is most closely tied to Autor, Dorn and Hanson. The skill-biased-change and education-technology race literature is tied to Katz. Dorn is a central co-author of the trade-shock work and is left out only because of the three-person limit. Katz's most famous education-technology work was done with a recent laureate, so his credit is somewhat overlapping.
assessment.maturity: The work spans roughly 1992 to 2016 and has been replicated, extended and debated for years. The task and trade-shock literatures are mature enough for a prize.
uncertainties: How to divide credit among the four credited names, and whether Dorn should replace Katz.
Debate over long-run persistence of the China shock and over how far the task framework explains wage polarization.
Possible overlap with recent prizes on labour economics and technology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Opened a large empirical literature on how legal origin, investor protection and institutions shape financial development and corporate governance. The cross-country evidence reorganized comparative finance and law-and-economics research and has had broad policy influence.
assessment.attribution: The core law-and-finance papers are by La Porta, Lopez-de-Silanes, Shleifer and Vishny. The legal-origins agenda was developed mainly by the first three. Vishny is a key co-author of the foundational papers but is left out here under the three-person limit. Shleifer's wider contributions in corporate finance and behavioural finance add to the case.
assessment.maturity: The work dates from the late 1990s and has had decades of scrutiny, replication and extension.
uncertainties: Serious methodological criticism of legal-origins classifications and of the causal interpretation of cross-country regressions.
Whether the committee prefers to reward Shleifer's broader body of work rather than this specific theme.
Selecting three of four credited names is a judgment call.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Built the modern analytical and empirical framework for how constitutions, electoral rules, state capacity and fiscal institutions shape policy and development. The work gave a unified theoretical foundation to political economics and inspired a large empirical agenda.
assessment.attribution: The Persson-Tabellini collaboration on constitutions and policy, and the Besley-Persson work on state capacity, are tightly linked. The three credited names cover the main contributions with clear and fairly distinct credit.
assessment.maturity: Foundational work dates from the 1990s and 2000s, with book-length syntheses and extensive follow-up. Highly mature.
uncertainties: Recent prize attention to institutions and political economy may reduce the near-term opening.
Some of the empirical results on electoral rules and fiscal outcomes are sensitive to identification assumptions.
Persson's role in the Swedish institutional context could raise conflict questions, which are disclosed rather than adjudicated here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Heterogeneous-agent New Keynesian models changed how macroeconomists analyse monetary and fiscal transmission by showing the importance of marginal propensities to consume and household balance sheets. They offer a tractable alternative to representative-agent frameworks and now shape policy modelling at central banks.
assessment.attribution: The three credited names are the clear core of the HANK synthesis (Kaplan-Moll-Violante 2018) and of related work on household heterogeneity. Violante also has earlier foundational contributions to heterogeneous-agent macro. Credit for the broader heterogeneous-agent tradition, which draws on earlier work by others, is not captured by the list.
assessment.maturity: The central paper is from 2018, so the field is relatively young. Adoption is rapid, but long-run validation is still incomplete.
uncertainties: Maturity is the main concern, since time has been short to test the framework's empirical performance.
Prior contributors to heterogeneous-agent macro may be seen as deserving credit.
The longlist treats this as a distinct discovery from the New Keynesian framework.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection moved international trade from industry-level to firm-level analysis. The framework explains export participation, productivity gains from trade and the within-industry reallocation that shapes how gains and losses are distributed.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the central contribution. Helpman, with Melitz and Yeaple, extended it to exporting versus foreign direct investment. Redding is a major contributor to quantitative and spatial extensions but is left out because of the two-name proposal. Helpman also appears under B017, and credit is not exclusive.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of confirmation across a very large empirical and theoretical literature. Mature.
uncertainties: Credit competition with Krugman-style new trade theory, already recognized, and with Eaton-Kortum approaches (see B011).
Whether Helpman's contributions are better recognized through B017 or this theme.
Whether a third laureate such as Redding would be warranted.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic panel GMM estimators are among the most widely used tools in applied economics, especially in growth, finance, industrial organisation and labour. They made it feasible to estimate dynamic relationships with unobserved heterogeneity and short panels.
assessment.attribution: Arellano-Bond (1991), Arellano-Bover (1995) and Blundell-Bond (1998) are the core papers, so credit is clear. Extensions by others (Anderson-Hsiao, Holtz-Eakin et al.) are not on the list.
assessment.maturity: Over thirty years of use. Mature and heavily validated, though also heavily critiqued in practice.
uncertainties: The committee's appetite for another pure econometric-method prize soon after 2021.
Known weak-instrument and proliferation problems in applied use, which could make the impact seem more mixed.
Blundell's additional contributions in labour and microeconometrics (see B048) overlap with this theme.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reconstructed long-run series on top incomes and wealth, putting distribution back at the centre of economics. This is the kind of historical data building that changes what we know, and it has had very large public and academic influence.
assessment.attribution: The top-income series program began with Piketty and with Piketty-Saez. Zucman extended it to wealth distribution and offshore wealth. A two-name proposal reflects the core income-series work, but whether Zucman should be included instead of, or in addition to, one of them is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: The income-share work dates from the early 2000s and has been widely extended. Methodological contestation is substantial.
uncertainties: Criticism of data construction, treatment of taxes and transfers, and the interpretation of wealth series.
Whether the committee values data-building and measurement over identified causal or theoretical findings.
Policy prescriptions associated with Piketty and Zucman may complicate the assessment, although the Nobel case rests on the empirical contribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showed with granular micro data that household leverage and credit supply expansions drove the housing boom and the depth of the Great Recession. This reshaped macro-financial thinking about credit cycles and distributional consequences of debt.
assessment.attribution: Mian and Sufi are clearly the central pair, with shared credit across the key papers and the synthesis book. John Y. Campbell's contributions to household finance and mortgage markets are more adjacent than central.
assessment.maturity: The central work dates from 2009 to 2014, over a decade ago, with mixed but generally supportive replication. Moderately mature.
uncertainties: Debate over causal identification of credit supply shocks and the relative weight of household debt versus other channels.
Possible overlap with the 2022 prize on banking and financial crises.
Maturity is shorter than for the other top-ranked candidates.
